outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_locks.py: new REVISIT_LIMIT = 3 (next to POLL_SECONDS); acquire counts `revisits` and the stamp-changed continue now fires only while revisits <= REVISIT_LIMIT, then falls through to the existing refusal (E_STALE). Requirement clauses: (1) bound the retry, count retries with a small cap: _locks.py REVISIT_LIMIT and the `revisits` counter in acquire. (2) pz3 goes red by assertion instead of hanging: test__locks.py pz3 now wraps judge with a counter and also asserts the claim was judged exactly once (the cap alone makes the over-fire end in the same E_STALE, so the answer cannot tell it from the real thing; the count can). (3) New case titled with the tests.add clause verbatim: a judge that replaces the claim on every ask (stops after 50 asks so a missing cap shows as a number, not a hang) must end E_STALE after more than 1 and at most 10 asks. (4) Run the unconditional-continue mutation once: ran via a script with mutation-landed asserts, __pycache__ purged between mutate and restore, 100s subprocess timeout, file restored (restored True). Mutation A (continue on every dead verdict, cap kept): exit 1, pz3 FAIL 137/138, no hang. Mutation B (cap removed, stamp test kept): exit 1, new case FAIL (judged 51 times), no hang. Honest limit: a mutation that deletes the cap AND the stamp test together is the original unbounded form and would still loop; the counter sits in the same block it guards. Full sweep exit 0, ruff and vermin clean.
outcome.descriptive: The retry in acquire is capped, so a regression that re-judges every dead claim now fails pz3 and the new case by assertion rather than hanging the suite.
